findings.title: /clear recreates record after failed close
findings.problem: handleSessionStart always calls createSessionRecord after closeClearedGeneration, which returns void and swallows its errors. When the close throws (e.g. a moveSetToGeneration failure that rolls back), the previous generation stays as {id}.json. A completed but undelivered one is then overwritten by the fresh record (saveSession to livePath), and an active one is re-entered and merged into the new generation. The task accepts the lock-timeout race; this error path is a separate trigger.
findings.impact: The previous generation's undelivered end metric and pending lines are lost, or two generations are merged into one record. Reachability of the throw path in practice was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Have closeClearedGeneration return whether the previous generation was moved aside, and skip createSessionRecord in handleSessionStart when it was not (at least on the error path), so a fresh record never overwrites an undelivered {id}.json or re-enters the previous generation.

findings.title: /clear lock check spawns ps in hook
findings.problem: closeClearedGeneration runs inside the `codemie hook` SessionStart process and acquires the reconcile lock in wait mode without pidOnlyLiveness. When the lock is contended, pid-lock.ts:80 judges the holder with isOwnerAlive, which spawns `ps` (1 s timeout) on each check during the wait of up to 10 s. handleSessionEnd (hook.ts:258) passes pidOnlyLiveness for hook processes, but this path does not.
findings.impact: The approved spec requirement (spec.md:254) that every lock check inside a hook process is pid-only and never spawns ps is not met on the /clear path. The SessionStart hook can spend extra time in ps calls and hold up the agent's session start.
findings.recommendation: Pass `pidOnlyLiveness: options.hookProcess === true` to acquirePidLock in closeClearedGeneration (as handleSessionEnd does at hook.ts:258), and add a test that the /clear path in a hook process never execs `ps`.

findings.title: No test pins hook-process pid-only sync lock
findings.problem: Regression gap: SessionSyncer picks pid-only liveness from context.hookProcess (set in delivery.ts:162; branch in isSyncLockStale at SessionSyncer.ts:140), but no test runs sync with hookProcess: true. A grep for hookProcess finds no test file, and SessionSyncer-lock.test.ts uses only the default context.
findings.impact: Consumer: syncPendingDataToAPI in the SessionEnd hook (delivery.ts:156-171). If the wiring or the pidOnly branch regressed, the hook would spawn ps inside its 2 s sync budget, or reclaim a lock whose live pid differs only by start time, and no test would fail.
findings.recommendation: In SessionSyncer-lock.test.ts, mock '@/utils/exec.js', write a lock { pid: process.pid, startedAt: 1 }, call sync with { ...context, hookProcess: true }, and assert no `ps` exec and a deferred result. Optionally, also assert that delivery.ts passes hookProcess: true.

findings.title: isProcessAlive EPERM change breaks daemon checks
findings.problem: isProcessAlive now returns true on EPERM (only ESRCH means dead), and this applies to every caller. checkStatus (daemon-manager.ts:67), the spawnDaemon readiness poll (daemon-manager.ts:137) and ensureOtlpProxy (connect-orchestrator.ts:453) now treat a recorded daemon pid reused by another user's process as a running daemon. Only stopDaemon was adapted. Evidence: EPERM tests exist only for stopDaemon and the helper itself (processes.test.ts:772-778).
findings.impact: After the daemon dies and another user's process reuses its pid, checkStatus reports running with stale state and ensureOtlpProxy skips starting a proxy, so OTLP hooks forward to a port nothing listens on. This change introduced the regression; it is not part of the out-of-scope EPMCDME-16545 daemon liveness work.
findings.recommendation: Keep EPERM meaning 'not our daemon' for daemon-state consumers (checkStatus, the spawnDaemon readiness poll, ensureOtlpProxy), either by handling EPERM there as stopDaemon does or by giving session-owner liveness its own helper. Add EPERM tests for checkStatus and ensureOtlpProxy that pin the intended outcome.
